title: Isometric translation of a type four coordinate into a disc algebra
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be fields [def-weil-field], complete for compatible nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute values, and suppose $k$ is algebraically closed. Let $z\in K\setminus k$ and suppose $K$ is the closure of the subfield $k(z)$. Put $r=\inf_{c\in k}|z-c|$ and assume $r>0$ and $|z-c|>r$ for every $c\in k$. Define $D_r(K)$ to be the ring of formal series $\sum_{n\geq0}a_nW^n$ with $a_n\in K$ and $|a_n|r^n\to0$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication, and put $\|\sum a_nW^n\|_r=\sup_{n\geq0}|a_n|r^n$. Regard $K$ as the constant series in $D_r(K)$. There exists a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $j:K\to D_r(K)$ such that $j(z)=z+W$ and $\|j(a)\|_r=|a|$ for every $a\in K$.

source.place: Section 6.2, printed p. 45, the two paragraphs immediately before Lemma 6.2.8: the disc description of completed scalar extension, specialized to l=K with the identity embedding.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-weighted-disc-banach] with $F=K$ and $s=r$. Write $B=D_r(K)$ and $\epsilon:B\to K$ for constant coefficient. Thus $B$ is a complete normed $k$-vector space and commutative normed ring, with submultiplicative norm, $\|W\|=r$, $\|a\|=|a|$ for constants, and $|\epsilon(f)|\le\|f\|$. These are exactly the positive-radius series and norm in the statement; restriction of the constant $K$-scalar action along $k\subset K$ gives the indicated $k$-action.

source.place: Printed p.45, disc algebra paragraph; explicit Banach input for the agent construction.

proof.text:
For a nonzero $P\in k[T]$, [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] writes $P(T)=a\prod_{i=1}^d(T-c_i)$ with $a
e0$ and $c_i\in k$, allowing $d=0$. Since $z
otin k$, all $z-c_i$ are nonzero, so $P(z)
e0$. This also proves that $z$ is transcendental and identifies the field $k(z)$ with fractions $P(z)/Q(z)$, $Q
e0$. Put $d_i=z-c_i$. Polynomial evaluation $T\mapsto z+W$ gives $P(z+W)=a\prod_i(d_i+W)$. Submultiplicativity and $\|d_i+W\|=\max(|d_i|,r)=|d_i|$ give $\|P(z+W)\|\le |a|\prod_i|d_i|=|P(z)|$. The reverse bound follows by applying constant coefficient $\epsilon$, so equality holds. For $P=0$ equality holds directly.

source.place: Printed p.45, first-factor polynomial map; agent factorization verification of its isometry.

proof.text: For every $c\in k$, put $d=z-c$ and $h=-W/d$. The hypothesis gives $\|h\|=r/|d|<1$. By [lem-trf-complete-normed-ring-geometric-inverse], $S=\sum_{n\ge0}h^n$ converges in $B$ and satisfies $(1-h)S=1$. Hence $(d+W)^{-1}=d^{-1}S$. Every finite geometric sum has norm at most $1$, by the ultrametric inequality and $\|h^n\|\le\|h\|^n$; passage to its norm limit gives $\|S\|\le1$. Thus $\|(d+W)^{-1}\|\le |d|^{-1}$. Factoring any nonzero $Q$ as in step 2 and multiplying these inverses proves $Q(z+W)$ is a unit and $\|Q(z+W)^{-1}\|\le |Q(z)|^{-1}$. Constant nonzero $Q$ is the empty-product case.

source.place: Printed p.45, polynomial-to-field passage in the first-factor map; geometric inverse argument made explicit.

proof.text: Define $j_0(P(z)/Q(z))=P(z+W)Q(z+W)^{-1}$. If two fractions agree, then $(PQ'-P'Q)(z)=0$; injectivity of evaluation at $z$, proved in step 2, gives $PQ'=P'Q$. Evaluate this polynomial equality at $z+W$ and multiply by the two denominator inverses to see that $j_0$ is independent of the presentation. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas now show that $j_0$ is a unital $k$-algebra map, fixes constants, and sends $z$ to $z+W$. Steps 2--3 give $\|j_0(x)\|\le|x|$. Applying $\epsilon$ to the inverse identities yields $\epsilon(j_0(x))=x$, so $|x|\le\|j_0(x)\|$. Consequently $\|j_0(x)\|=|x|$, and applying this to $x-y$ proves that $j_0$ is an isometry.

source.place: Printed p.45, first-factor map; elementary fraction construction from steps 2--3.

proof.text: The subfield $D=k(z)$ is a $k$-linear subspace dense in $K$ by hypothesis. The $k$-linear map $j_0:D\to B$ is contractive by step 4 and $B$ is complete by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] to obtain a continuous $k$-linear extension $j:K\to B$ with $j|_D=j_0$ and $\|j(a)\|\le|a|$. In particular $j(1)=1$ and $j(z)=z+W$.

source.place: Printed p.45, completion of the first-factor polynomial map; dense linear extension input.

proof.text: Fix $a,b\in K$ and choose $x_n,y_n\in D$ with $|x_n-a|<1/(n+1)$ and $|y_n-b|<1/(n+1)$, using density. Then $x_n,y_n$ are bounded and $|x_ny_n-ab|\le\max(|x_n||y_n-b|,|x_n-a||b|)\to0$. The same submultiplicative estimate in $B$ shows $j(x_n)j(y_n)\to j(a)j(b)$. Continuity and $j_0(x_ny_n)=j_0(x_n)j_0(y_n)$ therefore give $j(ab)=j(a)j(b)$ by uniqueness of metric limits. Together with the linearity and $j(1)=1$ this makes $j$ a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism. Finally $|\|j(a)\|-\|j_0(x_n)\||\le\|j(a)-j_0(x_n)\|\to0$ and $||a|-|x_n||\le|a-x_n|\to0$. Since $\|j_0(x_n)\|=|x_n|$, it follows that $\|j(a)\|=|a|$ for every $a$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q76-5631d0be0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 6 steps and the new node in full; no fixes. The Temkin PDF (§6.2, p.45) is not in the local literature (cited by 728 nodes), so I could not read the source at the cited place. The proof is self-contained (proof_origin agent), so I checked the statement and every step directly. The item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to Q159's creating version, and it is not a re-split item. The statement is true. The map on k(z) is forced: P/Q goes to P(z+W)/Q(z+W). ||z-c+W|| = |z-c| holds only because the distance r is never attained; at an attained distance 1+W/(z-c) would not be invertible, so the hypothesis is the needed one. Step 1: the new node with F=K, s=r; restricting scalars to k is fine. Step 2: the linear-factorization leaf; z not in k makes evaluation injective; upper bound by ultrametric and submultiplicative norms, lower bound through epsilon(P(z+W))=P(z). Step 3: the geometric-inverse leaf applied to h=-W/d with ||h||=r/|d|<1; the bound ||S||<=1 is proved in the step from partial sums. Step 4: well-defined by cross-multiplication, and an isometry because epsilon is a left inverse. Step 5: the dense-subspace extension leaf (extendOfNorm), with B complete, D=k(z) dense and j_0 contractive. Step 6: multiplicativity and the norm identity by density, with bounded approximants. New node lem-trf-weighted-disc-banach: statement-only, self-contained, true. I tested s=1, s<1, s>1, s outside the value group, a trivially valued F, f=0, constants and W. It is strictly smaller than the item and is not a restatement.
